solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Exact time to interrupt kiss

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so the time letter goes inside the kiss word

parts.note: to spoon is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Someone times a kiss precisely, cutting in at the perfect moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Spot on is an informal idiom for precisely correct, just as exact means.

clue.text: Extra tasty thing, face on beauty

indicators.note: on in a down clue means sitting above, so the face comes first

parts.note: a side is a face of a solid shape
a dish is informal for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A beauty's face is described in food terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A side dish is an extra item served alongside the main course of a meal.

clue.text: A couple of dismissals in total

definitions.meaning: two dismissals, an out and another out, as in cricket
complete or utter, as in an absolute villain

explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means utter or complete, and literally reads as two outs joined.

clue.text: Those in a parlour getting head shaved a lot

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, and shaving it off removes that letter

parts.note: poodles are the classic clients of a dog-grooming parlour

explanation.surface: Clients in a parlour are having their heads shaved in large numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The parlour is a dog-grooming salon, not a sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it matches a lot.

clue.text: Activate bad speller in boy

indicators.note: in places the spell-caster inside the word for a boy

parts.note: a son is a boy
a witch casts spells, often malign ones, so she is a 'bad speller'

explanation.surface: A boy who can't spell is being switched on to learning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad speller' suggests poor spelling, but it means a caster of evil spells.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch something on is to set it running, a plain synonym of activate.

clue.text: Grass wet, brollies out after wind and hail for starters

indicators.note: after places the jumble following the two first letters
for starters takes the first letters of wind and hail
out means put in disarray, so wet and brollies are rearranged

explanation.surface: After wind and hail, the grass is wet and umbrellas come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns WET BROLLIES into ISTLEBLOWER. Grass is British slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is British slang for an informer, and a whistle-blower exposes wrongdoing to authorities.

clue.text: Having the will, set up location for art

indicators.note: up in a down clue means reading upwards, so the word set is reversed

parts.note: the Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain, notably in London

explanation.surface: A determined artist sets up an exhibition space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' makes TES from SET; the Tate is Britain's national gallery of modern and British art.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate describes a person who dies having made a valid legal will.

clue.text: Boxer overcoming male in female quarters

indicators.note: overcoming in a down clue means sitting on top of, so the boxer goes above the male letter

parts.note: hares are known for boxing each other in spring

explanation.surface: A boxer beats a man inside the women's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter, but it is the animal that boxes in spring fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the women's section of a traditional Muslim household.

clue.text: Long-distance runner drinking pint after pint initially, as source of milk

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the river holds the two letters

parts.note: the Nile is a very long river, and rivers run

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each pint

explanation.surface: A marathon runner downs pint after pint of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-distance runner' is a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A teat on a mammal's breast is where milk is delivered to young.

clue.text: Old saw

definitions.meaning: saw in the sense of went out with romantically

explanation.definitionFit: Dated means both outmoded and having courted someone, the second a past tense like saw.

clue.text: First to prove after terrible crash, tin helmet securer?

indicators.note: after puts the first letter of prove at the end of the jumble
terrible signals the words crash and tin are wrecked into a new order
first to takes only the opening letter of the word prove

explanation.surface: A tin helmet is tested after a dreadful crash to see whether it holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' signals the anagram and 'after' places the first letter of 'prove' at the end; the question mark admits the definition is descriptive rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinstrap is the strap under the jaw that holds a helmet firmly in place.

clue.text: Change of air in the end with Queen opening event

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the phrase for the end

parts.note: 'curtains' is slang for the end, death or ruin

indicators.note: change of signals the word air is rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: A shift in atmosphere at the finale, with the Queen attending an opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of' signals the anagram, which 'in' sets just before the final S of the slang for the end; 'curtains' as the end is British idiom for finish or death.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a short piece or event that comes before the main attraction.

clue.text: Male in tights rent asunder

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, torn apart, so the following word is ripped into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's tights are torn to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' (torn) rearranges ASUNDER into DANSEUR; 'rent asunder' reads as one phrase but splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseur is a male ballet dancer, who typically performs wearing tights.

clue.text: Slow down, no thanks to metal behind vehicle

indicators.note: behind puts the trimmed metal after the vehicle

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle on rails

indicators.note: no says the word for thanks is to be absent from metal

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Metal fixed behind a vehicle slows it down, and nobody is grateful for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no thanks' removes TA from METAL, leaving MEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to hamper or restrict movement, which is to hold back or impede.

clue.text: Block vessels in retreat

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word for vessels is read in reverse

parts.note: pots are vessels

explanation.surface: Warships are blocked as they pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop something is to block or prevent it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Free-for-all in vehicle, one driving in the desert

indicators.note: in puts the brawl inside the word for a vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a melee is a confused free-for-all fight

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out in a car being driven through the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameleer is someone who drives or leads camels, which work in desert country.

clue.text: Above church, check for further support

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the other pieces on top of the church

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A building is checked above the church to see whether it needs extra support.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen by adding more backing, more support.

clue.text: God enters request for abundance

indicators.note: enters means going into, so the god goes inside the request

parts.note: a plea is a request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A god steps in to answer a request for plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or great amount of something.

clue.text: Confusion about sides in rhombi — this having one fewer?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the tangle goes round the edge letters

parts.note: a tangle is a muddle or confusion

indicators.note: sides in a word are its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: A puzzled geometry student muddles the sides of rhombi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides in rhombi' gives RI, its outer letters. A rhombus has four sides; the answer's shape has three, one fewer.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided figure has one side fewer than the four-sided rhombus, so the cryptic hint fits.

clue.text: Sudden attacks in part of Greece discussed

indicators.note: discussed means spoken, so the phrase is judged by its sound

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island, so in part of Greece is 'in Rhodes'

explanation.surface: Raids in a region of Greece are being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are raids or incursions into enemy territory, hence sudden attacks.

clue.text: Ring placed backwards

indicators.note: backwards says the word for placed is read from right to left

parts.note: laid means placed or put down

explanation.definitionFit: To dial is to ring someone on the telephone, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: River before sea is considered

indicators.note: before puts the river first

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A river flowing before the sea is thought of as a route.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem is to judge or regard, so deemed means considered.

clue.text: Nerve that's hit by a heavy drinker?

definitions.text: that's hit by a heavy drinker?

explanation.definitionFit: Bottle means courage in British slang, and a hard drinker is said to hit the bottle.

clue.text: Artier broadcast touring classy old Italian region

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the jumble goes round the classy letter
broadcast means scattered, so the word artier is thrown into a new order

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A more arty programme is broadcast while touring an upmarket old Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' makes ETRRIA from ARTIER; 'touring' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was the ancient land of the Etruscans in central Italy, now Tuscany and nearby areas.

clue.text: Five in number are required — more unlikely

indicators.note: five in says five letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Five in a number are needed, which is unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five' looks like a number, but it counts the letters picked out.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarer is the comparative of rare, so more seldom found and less likely.

clue.text: Cosmetic substance from tungsten and a lot of bananas

parts.note: W is the chemical symbol for tungsten

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the words a lot of go wild

explanation.surface: A cosmetic is said to come from a metal and plenty of bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges A LOT OF into OOLFAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool fat, or lanolin, is a grease from sheep's wool used in skin creams and cosmetics.

clue.text: Opener for England right after Germans out for a duck

indicators.note: after places the jumble before the opener and right letter
out means wrong or disordered, so the word Germans is rearranged
the opener for a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cricket report: England's opener is right after the Germans are out for a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GERMANS into MERGANS. In cricket a duck is a score of nought, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A merganser is a fish-eating diving duck with a slender serrated bill.

clue.text: Body temperature measured roughly

parts.note: a figure measured roughly is given approximately, 'or so'

explanation.surface: A nurse takes body temperature only approximately.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Delivery finally on order is terribly insulting

indicators.note: on means placed next, so the final letter is added after the jumble
terribly suggests things done badly, so order and is are scrambled
finally takes the last letter of the word Delivery

explanation.surface: A delivery that turns up badly ordered is insultingly poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' turns ORDER IS into DERISOR, then Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so small or poor as to be an insult, as in a derisory pay offer.

clue.text: Greek ship-launcher west of a US state capital

indicators.note: west of in an across clue means to the left, so the name comes before the letter

parts.note: Helen of Troy had 'the face that launched a thousand ships'

explanation.surface: A Greek woman who launched ships is placed west of a US state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena is the capital city of Montana in the north-western United States.
